thread:
ana: heads-up, spectra-lite int6 bring-up showed a weird pattern: recall@1 stable, but recall@10 dropped ~5% on our agglutinative-lang split. posting quick dump.
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] spectra-lite/int6 | evalset: agglut-holdout | recall@1: 0.881 -> 0.878 (-0.3%) | recall@5: 0.934 -> 0.912 (-2.3%) | recall@10: 0.967 -> 0.919 (-4.8%) | silhouette: 0.18 -> 0.09 (-0.09) | n=6,240
kevin: hmm, recall@10 drop with silhouette halving suggests cluster thinning not just center shift. any per-lang breakdown?
embed-eval-bot: per-lang: fi: recall10 -7.1%, hu: -6.2%, tr: -5.9%, en: -0.6%
ravi: those are agglutinative / morph-rich langs — tokenization granularity might interact with int6 LUTs. did we use symmetric clipping?
ana: used int6_asymmetric with default overflow=0.02. calibration samples=2k global.
lia: can we try per-lang stratified calib + asymmetric->symmetric flip and also test overflow sweep [0.01, 0.02, 0.05]? small nuance: asymmetric can bias heavy-tail tokens.
kevin: also run a prefix-cache simulation. in prod we enable prefix_cache_len=32 for streaming gen; our eval harness doesn't simulate it. prefix interactions changed attention norms in earlier bring-ups.
ravi: good call. i'll kick off three runs: (A) strat-calib 4k/lang + symmetric clip, (B) strat + asymmetric clip overflow 0.01, (C) same as B + prefix_cache_len=32. commands in case you want to mirror:

A: ./tools/embed_eval --model spectra-lite/int6 --calib-split stratified --calib-per-lang 4096 --quant-mode symmetric --seq 512 --dataset agglut-holdout --save-umap run/1789000000-A
B: ./tools/embed_eval --model spectra-lite/int6 --calib-split stratified --calib-per-lang 4096 --quant-mode asymmetric --overflow 0.01 --seq 512 --dataset agglut-holdout --save-umap run/1789000000-B
C: ./tools/embed_eval --model spectra-lite/int6 --calib-split stratified --calib-per-lang 4096 --quant-mode asymmetric --overflow 0.01 --seq 512 --prefix_cache_len 32 --dataset agglut-holdout --save-umap run/1789000000-C

lia: i'll add --k=1,5,10 and --cluster-metrics per-lang. also include median-distance histogram and top-10 confusion diffs.
embed-eval-bot: queued runs A,B,C (ETA ~30m)
kevin: when results arrive, plot UMAP diffs and a delta-CDF of pairwise distances. if small fraction of neighbors move beyond threshold that explains recall@10 shift.
ravi: quick preliminary thought: int6 asymmetric tends to preserve high-magnitude coordinates but compress midrange, which can stretch intra-cluster distances for long-tailed token distributions common in agglutinative morphs.
ana: ran a tiny local test with per-lang calib=3k asymmetric overflow 0.01: recall@10 improved to -2.1% vs fp16, silhouette 0.13. not perfect but better.
lia: that's promising. note to self: check token-level quant error grouped by normalized token frequency and by unicode category (accented/combining vs base).
kevin: good. also open INF-2412: spectra-lite onboarding — include required steps: stratified calib, overflow tuning, prefix_cache simulation, and UMAP review. assign to @ravi for runs, @lia for metric dashboards.
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] run 1789000000-A completed | recall@10 0.954 | silhouette 0.15
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] run 1789000000-B completed | recall@10 0.961 | silhouette 0.14
embed-eval-bot: [AUTO] run 1789000000-C completed | recall@10 0.959 | silhouette 0.13
ana: interesting: stratified helped a lot; asymmetric low-overflow slightly better on recall but symmetric gave better silhouette. prefix_cache had minor negative impact compared to B.
ravi: conclusion: default onboarding should require stratified calib 4k/lang and a small overflow sweep; prefer asymmetric overflow ~0.01 for recall-sensitive workloads, symmetric if we care about cluster compactness (downstream kNN latency).
lia: i'll update the onboarding checklist and add a note about simulating prefix_cache_len where applicable. i'll attach UMAPs and median-distance CDF plots to INF-2412.
kevin: solid. thanks all. :rocket:
